title: Axles and alignment
target: Use measurements and observations to improve straight rolling.
criteria: Check axle parallelism and wheel clearance.
Use evidence to choose one adjustment.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A model car drifts sideways in repeated unpowered roll tests. What should be checked first?
options: Axle parallelism and unequal wheel rubbing.
Whether the paint reflects light.
The motor voltage while disconnected.
Whether the switch label is large enough.
cpa.guide: Unpowered drift can reveal alignment and asymmetric friction without motor effects.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A wheel touches the chassis once each turn. Which change addresses this observation?
options: Double the battery voltage to hide the rubbing.
Call the wheel free because it clears at one angle.
Adjust the fit to maintain clearance throughout a full turn, then retest.
Add more contact pressure.
cpa.guide: Full-rotation clearance matters; periodic rubbing can create unequal resistance.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Which before-and-after free-roll comparison best tests an alignment adjustment?
options: Powered trials before and unpowered trials after.
Same ramp release, surface, and distance; several trials for each alignment.
Different slopes and a single trial each.
Only the best result from each design.
cpa.guide: Controls and repeats help separate alignment effects from test conditions and variation.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: Example offsets after the same forward travel are 9, 8, 10 cm before and 3, 4, 2 cm after one adjustment. What is supported?
options: The first readings were impossible.
The adjustment reduced sideways drift in these trials.
The adjustment doubled motor power.
The car will never drift again.
cpa.guide: Every after value is smaller; the evidence supports reduced drift under tested conditions, not universal guarantees.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A free-roll test shows rubbing only at the left rear wheel. Which next step best isolates a cause of drift?
options: Change wheels, battery, motor, and surface together.
Adjust only the paint pattern.
Record a better result without retesting.
Correct that contact and repeat the same test before changing other parts.
cpa.guide: One controlled change gives interpretable evidence about the observed asymmetric resistance.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: After an alignment revision, offsets remain 7, 8, and 7 cm; before they were 8, 7, and 8 cm. What is the strongest claim?
options: The car is perfectly aligned.
The readings prove no physical cause exists.
These results show little clear improvement; more diagnosis is needed.
The revision proved a large improvement.
cpa.guide: The overlapping ranges do not show a large reliable change. Check causes and measurement consistency.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
